texts.facts: This application is filed under section 11(6) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act by the petitioner against the respondents seeking appointment of an Arbitrator to resolve the dispute between the petitioner and the respondents. 2. The Respondent no.1 is MSTC Limited which is a Government Company engaged in the business of e-sale through e-auction of industrial by-products, scrap and wastage, etc. available for sale with Government and Semi Government Companies/Undertakings. It maintains a portal which can be utilized by Government organizations for selling their services /products. It is a mere service provider/agent of the advertiser organization. 3. Respondent no.2 is a Government of India undertaking engaged in the business of manufacture and sale of fertilizers from its factory and office situated at Sindri in the Dhanbad District of the State of Jharkhand. 4. The Respondent No.1 floated a tender inviting bids from prospective buyers for sale of Fly Ash and Bottom Ash belonging to Respondent No.2 lying in Chalk Pit Area between HURL boundary and ACC Company boundary of FCI Sindri Unit, Sindri through e-auction. 5. The portal of the respondent no.1 mentioned General terms and conditions of e-auction and M/S Absolute Vintrade Pvt. Ltd. Having ... vs M/S Mstc Limited on 21 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155247589/ 1 further buyers specific terms and conditions (BSTC). Anenxure-1 is a copy of the BSTC which contains the arbitration clause in Clause-3. It states: " 3.0. ARBITRATION In the event of any dispute or difference relating to the interpretation terms, text, application of the provisions of contracts, such dispute or difference shall be referred by either party for Arbitration to a sole Arbitrator to be appointed mutually by the parties. In case the parties fail to appoint the sole arbitrator within 30 days of the invocation of arbitration, the same will be appointed as per the provisions of the arbitration and Conciliation Act,1996...." 6. The Petitioner became a successful bidder after participating in the e-auction and was awarded contract through issuance of a sale order dt. 26.04.2022 by the Respondent No.1, acting as agent of respondent no.2. 7. According to the petitioner, during the execution of the work order, dispute arose between it and the respondent no.2 and so the petitioner sent a letter dt.19.1.2024 raising a dispute with the respondent no.2 requesting resolution of the same. 8. The respondent no.2 replied to the same quoting a clause relating to "INSPECTION" of the Tender and contending that they will not entertain the petitioners request. 9. Petitioner then wrote a letter dt.15.2.2024 to respondent no.2 specifically contending that the respondent no.1 ought to have agreed to resolve their dispute through arbitration and reiterating its request to resolve it through arbitration. 10. On 11.3.2024, the respondent no.2 replied to petitioner that there is no arbitration clause/ agreement in the sale order and therefore petitioners request cannot be acceded to. 11. Petitioner then got issued a legal notice dt. 12.03.2024 to both the respondents seeking appointment of an Arbitrator. 12. The Respondent no.1 sent a reply on 22.04.2024 denying the existence of dispute as well as the application of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,1996 for the purpose of appointment of an arbitrator for settlement of dispute and shifted the responsibility to the Respondent No.2 for settlement of the dispute. 13. Therefore, the petitioner has moved this Court for appointment of an Arbitrator. 14. After service of notice in this Arbitration Application, the Respondent No.1 filed a counter affidavit contending that it should be deleted from the array of parties because it is not a necessary party quoting clauses 16.11 and 16.12 of the BSTC. 15. The said clauses state as under: M/S Absolute Vintrade Pvt. Ltd. Having ... vs M/S Mstc Limited on 21 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155247589/ 2 "Clause 16.11. The bidder/buyer recognizes that the role of MSTC in the auction process is limited to that of a service provider/agent only and accordingly agrees not to make MSTC a party in any legal proceeding arising out of any dispute between the bidder/buyer and the seller/principal;
texts.arguments: Clause 16.12 : The buyer acknowledges and agrees that after issuance of delivery order, as per the terms and conditions governing the e-auction, MSTC shall have no role thereafter and under no circumstances shall be held liable for any issue arising out of or related to the quality, quantity, condition, possession or delivery of the material by the sellers/principals." 16. The counsel for the petitioner sought to contend that notwithstanding the same, the respondent no.1 (MSTC) continues to be liable and should be made party to the arbitration in view of the arbitration clause referred to supra. 17. I am unable to agree to the said contention in view of the specific provisions contained in Clauses 16.11 and 16.12 of the BSTC which limit the role of respondent no.1 only to that of a service provider and shifting the responsibility for any dispute with the Principal/FCI to the Principal only. Petitioner
